ADR security review fixes (#836)

* docs(adr): Apply security review findings to ADR 0023

Seven findings from security review (2026-06-24):
- Specify JCS/RFC 8785 canonical form as HMAC input to enable
  cross-language SIEM verification and prevent non-deterministic
  byte-ordering bypass
- Clarify from_cadf() is internal test-tooling only; document correct
  SIEM verification algorithm
- Require boot_session_id to be a CSPRNG UUIDv4 to prevent seq-gap false
  alerts across restarts from ambiguous session identity
- Add per-signal-type sanitization rules for attacker-controlled
  initiator.host (EC2 key, federation idp_id, generic pre-auth values)
- Fix refresh_hmac_key: remove non-atomic read-modify-write that could
  produce version collisions under concurrent rotation; caller now
  supplies new_version
- Add HMAC key retention policy (min 24h) and require SIEMs to cache all
  key versions for spool replay verification
- Require SIEMs to validate observer.node_id against ingestion source to
  detect cross-node spool injection (shared KEK means events are valid
  on any node)
- Fix map_event_to_action: Operation::Other arm returned &str borrowing
  a local String (dangling reference, compile error); now returns String
  directly

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(adr): Apply security review findings to ADR 0016-v2

Eight findings from a security-lens review of the Raft storage ADR:

- F1 HIGH: Widen Raft log nonce NodeId from 4 to 8 bytes (counter shrunk
  to 4 bytes). The 4-byte truncation caused nonce-space collision between
  nodes sharing the same lower 32 bits of their u64 NodeId — AES-GCM
  nonce reuse. Also names the HWM storage key (_meta:nonce_hwm:<node_id>).
- F2 MEDIUM: Make audit HMAC key per-node by including node_id_u64_be in
  HKDF info. Shared key allowed any compromised node to forge records for
  other nodes.
- F3 MEDIUM: Add dek_version_u32 to backup manifest AD. Without it, two
  backups taken in the same UTC second had identical manifest ADs and
  their manifests were swappable.
- F4 MEDIUM: Expand §4.1 SPIFFE mode with ≤1h SVID TTL ceiling,
  5-minute force-renewal window, fail-closed behaviour on SPIRE outage,
  and required SPIFFE ID pattern for gRPC interceptor validation.
- F5 MEDIUM: Specify quarantine state as Raft-committed and
  restart-persistent. In-memory-only quarantine was escapable via process
  restart, enabling repeated GCM probing.
- F6 LOW: Add explicit abort path for emergency rotation when the
  dual-control confirmation window expires without a ConfirmRotateDek.
- F7 LOW: Specify NodeId uniqueness check as fail-closed when no cluster
  member is reachable at startup.
- F8 LOW: Change sub-key derivation notation from HKDF-SHA256 to
  HKDF-Expand (Expand-only) to prevent implementors from running Extract
  over an already-uniform key.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(adr): Apply security review findings to ADR 0022

Addresses trusted proxy IP spoofing (new Invariant 9 + config section),
Retry-After thundering herd on sub-second waits (.max(1), Invariant 10),
Unicode homoglyph bypass in key normalization (NFKC added to Invariant
7), config value bounds enforcement, LRU eviction over fail-open for the
keyed store, and key-length validation guidance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(adr): Apply security review findings to ADR 0021

Four findings from a security-lens review of the API-key SCIM ADR:

- F1 MEDIUM: Add explicit NoAuthorizationsFound error when UME resolves
  to zero authorizations. Without this, hydrate_ephemeral_context
returned a valid ValidatedSecurityContext with ScopeInfo::Unscoped and
empty roles — a successful authentication — for any key whose mapping
was deleted or misconfigured. Fix: is_empty() guard before len() > 1
check.
- F2 MEDIUM: Rewrite §3 Step 2 to name the "rightmost non-trusted-proxy
  IP" XFF algorithm explicitly. The original text said "extract from XFF
if immediate upstream is trusted" without specifying which entry, making
a leftmost-take (XFF[0]) implementation plausible and exploitable for
allowed_ips bypass via an untrusted intermediate proxy. §6.E updated for
consistency. Invariant 4 added.
- F3 LOW: Specify that allowed_ips: None means "no restriction" (not
  deny-all). Added inline struct comment, noted in §3 Step 2 and §6.E,
and Invariant 5.
- F4 LOW: Specify that compute_deterministic_user_id must take client_id
  (not provider_id) as input. During N:1 rotation two keys share a
provider_id; a provider_id-derived user_id would conflate audit records.
Invariant 6 added.

New §7 Security Invariants section formalises all eight invariants
(including system-scope prohibition, single-scope constraint, and
dummy-hash timing parity) that were previously only described in prose.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+- F4 MEDIUM: SPIFFE mode expanded with TTL ceiling, fail-closed behaviour, SPIFFE ID pattern (§4.1)
+- F5 MEDIUM: Quarantine state specified as Raft-committed and restart-persistent (§10 invariant 5)

 Keystone-NG requires a storage backend providing high availability, strong

@@ -131,17 +143,19 @@ AES-256-GCM requires strict nonce uniqueness. Truncated tags are prohibited; all
 tags must be 16 bytes.
 
 - **Raft Log (Log DEK):** Nonce is
-  `[4-byte NodeId BE] ++ [8-byte monotonic counter BE]`. The counter is stored
-  durably and increments with a reservation block of 1024 to absorb crashes. On
-  startup, the persisted counter is validated against a separately-stored
-  high-water mark; if the recovered counter is less than or equal to the high-
-  water mark, the node refuses to start and requires operator intervention,
-  preventing nonce reuse from counter corruption. After each reservation block
-  write, the node verifies the write by reading back and comparing; if the
-  read-back does not match, the node treats it as a fatal storage error and
-  halts, preventing silent nonce reuse during a live session. A warning is
-  emitted when remaining counter space drops below 10% of the `2^31` rotation
-  threshold.
+  `[8-byte NodeId BE] ++ [4-byte monotonic counter BE]`. NodeId occupies the
+  full 8 bytes (matching the `u64` type in §8) to prevent nonce-space collision
+  between nodes that share the same lower 32 bits. The counter is stored durably
+  and increments with a reservation block of 1024 to absorb crashes. On startup,
+  the persisted counter is validated against a separately-stored high-water mark
+  (kept in a dedicated Fjall metadata key `_meta:nonce_hwm:<node_id>`); if the
+  recovered counter is less than or equal to the high-water mark, the node
+  refuses to start and requires operator intervention, preventing nonce reuse
+  from counter corruption. After each reservation block write, the node verifies

+  node treats it as a fatal storage error and halts, preventing silent nonce
+  reuse during a live session. A warning is emitted when remaining counter space
+  drops below 10% of the `2^31` rotation threshold.

@@ -246,12 +260,17 @@ independently of the identity data store.

+- **Identity:** Short-lived X.509 SVIDs rotated automatically. SVID TTL MUST

+- **SPIFFE ID Pattern:** All Keystone storage node SVIDs MUST match

@@ -336,6 +369,11 @@ any existing member shares the same `node_id` but has a different `rpc_addr`, a

     pub client_id: String,             // Public UUID for management API references
     pub lookup_hash: String,           // Fast SHA-256 hash of the token for O(1) DB index lookups

 1. The middleware queries FjallDB for
    `data:api_client:v1:<domain_id>:<lookup_hash>`.

-3. It extracts the source IP from `X-Forwarded-For` **only** if the immediate
-   upstream connection matches an explicitly configured `trusted_proxies` array
-   (otherwise falling back to the raw TCP peer IP). It then validates this IP

@@ -134,11 +152,21 @@ operate under exactly _one_ scope.
 
 ```rust
 pub async fn hydrate_ephemeral_context(...) -> Result<ValidatedSecurityContext, AuthenticationError> {
-    let user_id = compute_deterministic_user_id(...);
+    // Derived exclusively from client_id (the unique key UUID), never from
+    // provider_id, so each API key produces a distinct audit identity even

+    let user_id = compute_deterministic_user_id(resource.client_id);

+    // the access decision entirely onto downstream OPA policy coverage.

+        return Err(AuthenticationError::NoAuthorizationsFound);
+    }
+

         return Err(AuthenticationError::MultipleScopesForbidden);
@@ -285,10 +313,14 @@ traffic migrates seamlessly, and Key A is subsequently revoked.
 ```
